title: Freya Bank Brief A phone-agent policy IR

rules.policy: Freya Bank and all customer, debt and payment data are fictional.
The specification requires complete clause coverage.
Handle one product 1–45 days overdue through identification, verification, debt disclosure, promise negotiation and closure.
actions: Seek a valid promise where possible

rules.policy: Only the supplied call variables are known before tool responses.
actions: Do not assume account or identity facts

rules.policy: Use supplied customer identity variables and now for addressing, tool arguments and all date calculations.
actions: Address customer as title plus last_name
Use supplied now, never the real clock
Do not promote example values into policy

rules.policy: Open with digital-assistant, Freya Bank and recording disclosures while withholding collection and account content until verification.
actions: Say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank and the call is recorded
Do not say collections, debt, payment or the product before both security questions pass

rules.policy: Ask whether the speaker is the named customer.
Allow two customer-name asks, accepting only explicit self-identification.
actions: Accept yes, that's me, speaking or customer's own name
Do not accept hello, go ahead or who is this
Answer AI or scam question before the next ask
Count the following ask as ask two
After second unclear response close not_reached/unclear

rules.policy: Answer AI or robot questions by identifying yourself as Freya Bank's digital assistant.
actions: Say you are Freya Bank's digital assistant

rules.policy: Give third parties no calling-purpose disclosure and ask when the customer can be reached.
actions: Limit disclosure to the opening sentence
exceptions: Required callback handling and deceased response

rules.policy: Schedule only a future callback today or the next business day within inclusive calling hours.
actions: Validate against supplied now and calendar
Send date and time to schedule_callback

rules.policy: Allow one replacement proposal after an invalid callback time.
actions: If replacement is invalid, do not schedule

rules.policy: End a wrong-number call as not reached.
rules.trigger: Number does not belong to customer

rules.policy: Express condolences and ask nothing further when told the customer has died.
actions: Say: I am sorry for your loss.

rules.policy: Relatives cannot complete security checks or receive account information, even when offering payment.
actions: Do not accept proxy security answers

rules.policy: Verify date of birth before phone last four, one question at a time, using normalized answers.
actions: After date-of-birth pass, ask phone last four
Use verified and all_verified results; ok alone is not verification
Unreadable date rejection is not a wrong answer

rules.policy: Three wrong security answers across both questions exhaust identity checking.
actions: Permit another ask while budget remains
Stop checking at three wrong answers
exceptions: Swapped-date hint and unreadable-date rejection do not consume budget

rules.policy: A swapped day/month hint requires a month-word clarification without consuming a wrong answer.
actions: Ask customer to say month as a word

rules.policy: After three wrong answers, withhold debt disclosure and direct the customer to the app or a branch.
actions: Tell customer to use mobile app or branch

rules.policy: Explain security once after refusal and close after a second refusal or calling-purpose question.
rules.trigger: Customer declines security or asks call purpose instead
actions: Count both response types toward the same refusal limit
First occurrence: explain questions protect the account

rules.policy: Retrieve account data only after both security questions pass.
actions: Use account data only from a successful response

rules.policy: Disclose collections purpose, product, past-due amount and days late from retrieved account data.
rules.trigger: Verified identity and successful account retrieval
actions: Say you are calling from collections about a late payment
For credit card, use returned card_last4

rules.policy: Use weekdays excluding the listed Freya Bank holidays as business days.
Determine each product's promise deadline from its days late.
Apply the band-specific business-day deadline and persuasion limit.
actions: Early: twelfth business day after today, one attempt
Late: seventh business day after today, two attempts

rules.policy: A promise date must be a business day between today and the deadline inclusive.
rules.trigger: Any proposed or revised promise date
actions: Validate date before confirmation or recording

rules.policy: Offer the next business day for an eligible weekend or holiday proposal.
rules.trigger: Non-business proposal on or before deadline
exceptions: Original proposal after deadline follows brief-a:23

rules.policy: Ask once for an exact date after a vague period, then propose the deadline if still unspecified.
Resolve this weekday in the current calendar week and next weekday in the following week.
Replace an after-deadline proposal with the deadline and count its rejection as flat refusal.
actions: Say latest recordable date is deadline

rules.policy: Propose the full past-due amount first and never ask how much the customer can pay.
actions: Do not ask: how much can you pay?
exceptions: Accept eligible unsolicited amounts under brief-a:27

rules.policy: Use minimum_payment as the credit-card floor and instalment_amount as the loan floor.
actions: Derive floor from retrieved product fields

rules.policy: Offer the floor once after full-amount unaffordability and explain that the remainder stays overdue.
rules.trigger: Customer says full amount is too much
actions: Treat floor rejection as flat refusal
exceptions: Late-band attempt two may offer floor again on deadline

rules.policy: Accept unsolicited amounts within the inclusive floor-to-full range and counter below-floor amounts once.
actions: Accept floor through past_due as proposed amount
Below floor: say amount cannot be recorded and offer floor once
Treat failure to accept floor as flat refusal

rules.policy: Start payment solicitation by asking for payment today.
actions: Ask: Can you make this payment today?

rules.policy: A customer-proposed date or amount is not itself a refusal.
actions: Do not consume persuasion attempt merely for proposal
exceptions: Subsequent rejection of the required deadline or floor follows brief-a:23, brief-a:26 or brief-a:27

rules.policy: Use bounded persuasion after flat refusals or non-answers with the prescribed amount and date.
actions: No to today without date or amount is flat refusal
Consume one persuasion attempt per applicable refusal or non-answer
Attempt one: full amount, or floor if full already unaffordable
Attempt one date: last business day this week; if today is that day, use next week's last business day
Late-band attempt two: floor on deadline
Keep all offers within date and amount constraints

rules.policy: Stop after permitted persuasion and do not repeat rejected offers.
actions: Do not repeat a refused offer
exceptions: Explicit floor reoffer permitted by brief-a:26 for late-band attempt two

rules.policy: Prioritize compassionate support over persuasion or restructuring while permitting voluntary valid promises.
rules.trigger: Illness, family death or job loss mentioned
actions: Acceptance: transfer to support and close transferred/support
For voluntary date or amount, complete validation, confirmation and recording
exceptions: Voluntary promise remains available under ordinary promise gates

rules.policy: Never offer discounts, waivers, instalment plans or unsupported terms.
Obtain a clear yes after product, amount and date readback before recording.
actions: Mark confirmed only after clear yes
Call create_promise only for the confirmed tuple

rules.policy: Revalidate and reconfirm every date or amount change made during confirmation.
Allow one recorded promise per product and no same-call change or cancellation.
actions: Do not create a second promise for that product
Do not change or cancel recorded promise
Tell requesting customer they can change it in mobile app

rules.policy: Treat a promise as recorded only on ok:true and retry a failed recording once.
actions: Second failure: say you could not record it and close no_promise/service_error
Do not equate proposed or confirmed state with recorded state
Later failures do not undo successful commits

rules.policy: Speak the required text-message statement after successful recording.
actions: Say: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.

rules.policy: For claimed payment of the current past-due amount, explain posting delay and take no promise.
rules.trigger: Customer says current arrears already paid
actions: Say payments can take one business day to appear
exceptions: Historical payoff or product closure is a dispute under brief-a:40

rules.policy: Treat denied ownership, historical payoff or historical product closure as dispute without argument or promise.
exceptions: Payment of current past-due amount follows brief-a:39

rules.policy: Transfer payment-plan or lower-instalment requests to restructuring without describing a plan.
rules.trigger: New plan or lower instalments requested

rules.policy: Offer help once after a human request and transfer to general if the customer insists.
rules.trigger: Human requested at any identity stage
actions: Ask once whether you can help first
If insistence continues, transfer to general

rules.policy: Answer scam concerns with the bank customer-service verification route and continue.
actions: Say customer can verify by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number

rules.policy: Admit unavailable information rather than inventing figures, dates or reasons.
actions: Say you do not have that information

rules.policy: End after two statements declining conversation, using the identity-appropriate outcome.
rules.trigger: Second statement that customer does not want to talk
actions: Handle human requests before or after verification under brief-a:42

rules.policy: Issue exactly one close_call as the final operation with the required outcome and reason.
actions: For all operations, ok:false means action was not carried out

rules.policy: Use only the listed outcome/reason combinations and their source-linked conditions.
actions: Use promise when at least one promise was recorded
Omit reason for promise and paid
Supply listed reason for every other outcome
exceptions: Transfer after recorded promise follows brief-a:closing.p2

rules.policy: A transfer after a recorded promise determines closure while preserving the promise.
Never use add_note in Brief A.
Thank the customer and say goodbye before the final closure operation.

stages.name: opening_and_customer_identification
stages.entry_gate: Call starts with supplied variables only.
stages.exit_gate: Explicit customer self-identification, third-party branch or terminal outcome; self-identification alone does not permit account disclosure.

stages.name: third_party_callback
stages.entry_gate: Someone other than the customer answers.
stages.exit_gate: Callback branch or another not_reached outcome; no security checks or account disclosure.

stages.name: security_verification
stages.exit_gate: Date of birth and phone last four both pass, or verification/transfer terminal branch; never retrieve or disclose account before both pass.

stages.name: account_retrieval_and_disclosure
stages.exit_gate: Successful account response supports product, amount and delinquency disclosure; account failure handling remains unresolved.

stages.name: product_negotiation
stages.entry_gate: Verified customer and successfully retrieved product.
stages.exit_gate: Valid proposed product/amount/date tuple or terminal branch; proposals are not confirmed or recorded.

stages.name: confirmation_and_recording
stages.entry_gate: Valid proposed tuple and no recorded promise for that product.
stages.exit_gate: Full readback and clear yes precede recording; only ok:true commits; one failed-call retry permitted; changes require revalidation and reconfirmation.

stages.name: post_recording
stages.entry_gate: Promise successfully recorded and required text-message sentence spoken.
stages.exit_gate: Recorded promise stays immutable; later transfer selects transferred outcome without cancelling the commit.

stages.name: closing
stages.entry_gate: Applicable terminal condition selected; thank customer and say goodbye.
stages.exit_gate: Exactly one close_call issued as final operation; no subsequent tool calls.

ambiguities: Only Brief A is supplied; no explicit amendment or inheritance source exists to resolve additional precedence.
Failure handling and retry limits for verify_identity, get_account, schedule_callback and transfer_to_agent are unspecified; OpenAPI permits repeating HTTP 500 calls but does not mandate a policy.
A failed close_call creates tension between OpenAPI retry permission and exactly one final close_call; no recovery rule is supplied.
The callback and transfer branches prescribe their terminal outcomes without defining what to do when the prerequisite operation fails; failed operations must not be represented as successful.
Brief A assumes one product, but get_account returns an array; selection or continuation when multiple products or no products are returned is unspecified.
A calendar week's starting day and the timezone of now are not explicitly defined.
Dates before today, amounts above past_due, missing product fields and inconsistent floor/past_due values lack corrective handling.
The first payment ask proposes today even when today is not a business day; the compliant alternative is unspecified.
The attempt-one weekly date may exceed the deadline, and attempts may produce an already-refused identical offer; no alternate proposal is authorized.
Whether floor-offer limits are shared across the unaffordability and below-floor branches, and whether repeated vague proposals share one clarification budget, is unspecified.

The wording of persuasion exhaustion does not explicitly distinguish issuing the final permitted offer from receiving its rejection; no immediate closure should be inferred while its response is pending.
Overlapping security refusals and statements declining conversation have separate stated limits but no explicit shared-count rule.
The voluntary-promise hardship exception does not fully specify sequencing when a support decision and a voluntary proposal occur together.
Hardship explicitly precedes persuasion and restructuring, and transfer explicitly outranks a recorded-promise outcome; other simultaneous terminal-condition priorities are unspecified.
Paid, dispute, hardship or refusal claims after successful recording have no explicit outcome priority against the recorded-promise table condition; the existing commit cannot be undone.

Rule 5's literal instruction to say nothing beyond the opening coexists with mandatory availability questions, callback handling and condolences; the permitted disclosure limit is clear, but the full allowed third-party dialogue is not enumerated.
Repeated swapped-date hints, unreadable dates and verification service errors have no retry ceiling in the supplied policy.
Freya Bank's customer service number and the payment currency are not supplied and must not be invented.
